But I don't remember exactly about this last meeting; this is why I do not want to refer to it here and now.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Let me take one of those, please. The meeting you said just now, there was a meeting in Medjugorje with Colonel Sporzo [phoen] -- Zorzo. Sorry, my apology. What did you understand, if you did, of Tuta's role in that meeting?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL
utterances.text: I did not exactly understand that he was a chief of a specific unit. He was an organiser within the military.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Well, can you tell us, were all the other persons in this meeting, were they all military persons? Were they all military officers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And going back to Mr. Andabak, do you recall how Mr. Andabak referred to Tuta? Did he describe him in any military terms or refer to him in any way as a superior?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Will you tell us what he said?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL
utterances.text: Well, according to a document that was done after the dinner party, a report I put forward, Mr. Tuta was a sort of chief and instructor of Ivan Andabak and the forces under him. He was over him. This is what I understood from Mr. Tuta.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Now, before turning to some documents, the last topic I want to ask you about is the Croatian army; that is, the HV, as opposed to the HVO. Can you tell the Chamber, please, during your tour of duty in Bosnia in 1993, did you ever see any HV forces or soldiers in the Spanish Battalion's area of responsibility?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL
utterances.text: Yes, in one opportunity, I could see that the roads leading to Mostar from the -- Ploce through Capljina, Ljubuski, I could see trucks with the name "HV" on them, and soldiers holding this marking with initials of HVO.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I'm sorry, did you mean to say HV --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: HV. The interpreter made a mistake.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL
utterances.text: HV.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Is it correct, sir, that you left this particular peacekeeping mission on about the 15th or 16th of July, 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL
utterances.text: Yes. The 16th of July, I got to Spain.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. Now, Witness, for the last part of your direct examination, I'd like to take you to a few documents. And I think there's a binder there that I hope all of them will be in.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And for the rest of the courtroom, Mr. President, I'm going to begin with Volume 1 of the SpaBat documents that I hope everyone will have available, as we previously had mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And if you can find first of all, Witness, Exhibit P301. And you can, of course, direct your attention to the Spanish version. And can you confirm just by looking at this document, for example, that this is a record that was made by the Spanish army during your tour of duty in Bosnia in 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL
utterances.text: Yes. It was made by the Spanish army on the 16th of April, 1993. It's a document that is an INTREP; it's a summary of information.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Directing your attention to -- it's not a long -- in the Spanish in particular, it's not a long document. But there's a paragraph that talks about certain actions in Doljani, Sovici. I believe it's approximately the third paragraph of the document, probably in either English or Spanish, the third paragraph, starting with "The main reason for the visit was to make very serious representations for help and in order to evacuate some 600 Muslims civilians." Now, can you tell me whether your unit was involved in collecting that information and played a role in, in fact, preparing this report?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Would you go, please -- we'll take one exhibit out of order. We'll skip over it and come back to it. Would you please go to 320 -- I'm sorry, I'm wrong about that. 325, please. Just go to 325. Looking at that document, sir, can you please assist the Chamber by confirming - again, if you can - this was a report made by the Spanish army in approximately April 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL
utterances.text: Yes. This was made by the Spanish army, our patrols.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Now, directing your attention to the document itself, you may be able to assist us with a couple of details. In these reports, there is a date and time of completion. And I'm looking at page 3 of the English -- top of page 3 of the English version. And it's a detail, but it may come up in some context and it may assist the Chamber. To the right of the entry date and time of completion, there is a series of numbers, "220105B APR93." Can you tell the Chamber, please, whether that indicates the date of the 22nd of April, 1993.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL
utterances.text: Yes. This document is a summary of the information concerning the 22nd day of April. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And what is the additional information? Between the "22" and the abbreviation for April, there is the "0105 B."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL
utterances.text: 1-0 [as interpreted] is the hour, 22nd of April at 10 [as interpreted] hours, and 5 minutes. "B", Bravo, is the hour, according to the summertime hour. It could be Alpha, it could be Bravo according to whether it's wintertime or summertime. And it has to do with the solar hours, Zulu.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Does this indicate that this report was actually prepared at 1.05 a.m. summertime?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL
utterances.text: Yes. It is the time in which the document was closed. We refer to the hour in which the document is closed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: You were working very late, sir.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL
utterances.text: Yes. I think that in these circumstances, we didn't really count hours in order to work and in order to establish contacts and give help to everybody.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Let me direct your attention, please, to page 5 in the English version, but it's under the section called -- titled "Jablanica." And directing your attention under that, and there's a number of entries, some of them rather short, but I think it would be about the sixth entry, if you will, or paragraph under "Jablanica" starting with the words "According to intelligence received ..." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL
utterances.text: Yes, it was me, personally, who drafted this information.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: These are your words, sir? Is that what you're telling us?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL
utterances.text: Yes. This expression and these data could only be known by myself; nobody else.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: So when you say here -- I'm going to just make reference to this statement and ask you some questions about it. You reported, then, on the 22nd of April, 1993: "The offensive is directed by a person of substantial political" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Meek. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, we again come to a situation where I believe the documents speak for themselves. And we are now in a situation where Mr. Scott wants to read these documents into the record, or he is going to ask this witness to read these documents line by line, word by word. I believe this is improper. I object. If he wants to ask a direct question and have a direct answer, it's a different situation. That's my objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Meek, that's a speculation of the question. We have not heard the question yet. That's the first. Secondly, this witness is the drafter of this document. We are very interested to hear the comments from this witness about this document so that we could know at least the authenticity of this document. Mr. Scott, are you going to read a substantial paragraph from this document?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I wasn't going to read a long passage, Your Honour, a few sentences, but I'll accommodate my learned friend.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: If I can simply ask, Witness LL, if you will look at that paragraph and take a moment to read that to yourself, I'll ask you a question or two.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL
utterances.text: Yes, I'm looking at it now.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: On what information did you have at this time that this person who is tired of signatures and political treaties, that this person is Tuta?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL
utterances.text: Yes, it's Mr. Tuta.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Can you assist the Chamber in telling it a bit more about the reasons you came to this conclusion and you included these statements in your report?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL
utterances.text: Normally before I write something such as this, one has to be quite sure what one is writing. This was an information, direct information from a source, military source of the BH [as interpreted] who -- or who is very close to Tuta and who gave me all the details on how this operation was going to be carried out.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Now, you just said - and I want to be clear whether it's again a translation or transcription error - this "source," and at this moment I'm not pressing you to identify the source specifically, but was this source affiliated with one side or the other or one of the military formations or the other?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL
utterances.text: Yes. The source is associated to the HVO.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And -- I'll leave it at that. Well, let me ask it this way: This information, do you recall whether that -- whether this date, the 22nd of April, was after your dinner conversation with Tuta and Andabak at Mr. Andabak's house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL
utterances.text: Yes. It was after that meeting, after that dinner party that I obtained this piece of information, later.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And so can you tell the Chamber, please, the information that's reported in this Exhibit 325 that we've been looking at for the last few moments, did you find that to be consistent with what Mr. Andabak and Mr. Tuta told you at this dinner?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL
utterances.text: Yes, it does coincide. The actions coincide with the intentions as expressed during the dinner party.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: If I could then ask you, please, to go to Exhibit 327. Can you tell us what Exhibit 327 is?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL
utterances.text: This is a file which was compiled on Mr. Tuta, that is, based on his -- about his biography and his personality.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Who prepared this document?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL
utterances.text: This document was prepared by the second section of the Main Staff on the basis of reports which I had procured myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Well, let me ask you this: Other than not preparing or not writing the words on the page, if I can ask this question this way: Who was the principal source - I don't mean the ultimate source but the information given to the Spanish army for the purpose of preparing this document - who was the principal provider of information, of this information?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL
utterances.text: This document is the fruit of information that was openly given us during the dinner in Ivan Andabak's house, where there was Tuta and Colonel Zorzo.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Now, if I can direct your attention, please, to the part of the document down -- that's in sort of a box. There's three columns. And in the far left column, there is the date of "7 April 1993." Can you assist the Chamber, please, in indicating is that the approximate date of the dinner with Tuta and Andabak?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL
utterances.text: Yes. It must have taken place one or two days later before that; that is, this is the time that I needed to compile the report and send it to the second section of the General Staff -- of Main Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: So as an example, up above that when it says: "Current Situation, chief instructor, he receives direct orders from Petkovic," and then later on you give information about his family, can you confirm to the Chamber, please, that this information or most of this information was stated to you by Tuta himself?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL
utterances.text: Yes. I repeat that that dinner was very relaxed. It was, one could say, a familiar -- atmosphere as amongst members of family. So we could talk about everything. And I saw the identity card, at least the identity card which at that time he had, and some lettering, and I remember that all the information was direct and it merely emerged from the conversation between this gentleman, that is, Mr. Tuta, Ivan Andabak, and representatives of Spain, Colonel Zorzo and myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Let's move on to Exhibit 357.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, in -- this particular document will not be -- I think it should be in the witness's binder for the witness stand purposes, but in the -- for everyone else in the courtroom, it was in this separate collection that was distributed previously, I believe - I hope - and it's Exhibit P357. And this document is under seal, so I'm not going to -- we haven't put any of them on the -- on the ELMO, but I want to identify it specifically, but it is Exhibit P357.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL
utterances.text: Yes. This is an INTREP dated 29 April, which was done at and closed at 2150.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Can I direct your attention, please, to again the information under the heading "Jablanica"? And directing your attention to the entry that says: "Fifty per cent of the city of Doljani ...."

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'll defer to the Chamber's own review of the Spanish, original Spanish document. I respectfully submit that in the Spanish version, the letter "D" is rather obvious, but for some reason it was transcribed "B," but of course the Chamber will decide.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: But you said: "Fifty per cent of the city of ..." to avoid controversy, I'll simply say here, "... Boljani is destroyed. The town of Sovigi seemed to be covered with smoke from a certain vantage point." Now, do you know again if this was information drawn on observations by your unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL
utterances.text: Yes. This was direct observation of my patrols about -- from this vantage point, and they made an information on these two places from this vantage point, which would cover both Doljani and Sovici.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And looking to the next item, "Comment."

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Which again I believe, Your Honours, it says "HVI." I submit to you the Spanish is rather -- obviously it says "HVO."

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Can you confirm to the Chamber that in fact these components of the Spanish army were stopped by the HVO to prevent them from seeing what was happening in Doljani and Sovici?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL
utterances.text: Yes. As I have already said earlier we could not move freely, not -- so that it was quite natural that we were not allowed to -- we were not given access to certain places, and our convoys at times were not allowed to go through.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Can we go next briefly to Exhibit 361, which should be back in the main binder. 361. It's a rather longer document, but when you have that, would you please, first of all, find the section that's -- section 1.3, "Neretva Valley." And if you can just cast your eyes down that page and the next, which again, among other things, mentions Sovici and Doljani. Can you confirm to the Chamber -- well, can you say one way or the other was this information again based upon information coming from the Deep Reconnaissance Patrol?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL
utterances.text: Before here we have a summary of information, that is, this is an INTSUM which recapitulates the reports between the 16th and the 30th of April. This is the summary of information, and it is based on the daily summaries of information collected in the area of operations, so that this document is based on the summaries of information collected daily in the area of operations, in the zone of operations.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Now, if I can direct your attention, please, to -- it will be on page 7 in the Spanish version, the second paragraph on page 7, and in the English version, the second full paragraph starting on page 8. It simply is a point of reference only. "There are reports that the HVO forces in this area are led by Tuta." Can you tell the Chamber again the information -- what this information is based upon?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL
utterances.text: This information is based on another information which I personally obtained from HVO sources, from military sources very close to Mr. Tuta.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. I think I won't -- for the interest of time, I won't stay on that any longer. Can we go to Exhibit 375, please? If you have that, sir, and again, you can just confirm that this is a Spanish army report? In fact, if we look at the content of the report, under "Mostar," does that reflect some of the information that you've told us about this morning in terms of what was observed happening in Mostar at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL
utterances.text: Yes. This document, unlike those others, was drawn up by the third section of the Main Staff, and that was the operative section, and this is a report on the situation, and that is why it is called a SITREP. And it is based on the summary of information provided by my patrols --

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Well, just to --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL
utterances.text: -- deployed in the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Just to take one example, because we're not going to spend much time on these documents now, but under "Mostar," the -- the four -- it would be the third -- there's some unbulleted paragraphs or items. But the third bullet saying: "A concentration of civilians has been seen in the football ground and transfer of the same civilians by bus out of the city," is that what you yourself, sir, observed on the 9th of May, 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL
utterances.text: Yes. This is based on my personal observation.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. President, I'm seeing if we can just perhaps skip a couple of these documents in order to conclude the witness before the lunch break.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: If we can go -- let's go to 401. And looking at that document, is that another report prepared or at least contributed to by your unit? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And, for instance, under the heading 1.2, "Areas in Mostar," did it indicate that, for instance, on the 17th of May, 1993 between 800 and 1.000 shells exploded in the -- most of them in the Muslim quarter on that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL
utterances.text: Yes. We had some observation posts from which we controlled the falling of the projectiles.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Directing --

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, there's a number of points we could stop on, but I'll leave it to the Chamber, of course, to be able to review the document for itself. I'm going to be very selective.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Witness, if I can ask you to go to the next -- I'm not sure if it's the next page in Spanish. But continuing on down the items under "Mostar," you will get to two starred -- if I can use -- starred items right above the section, then, beginning "Jablanica." And there's a reference there -- the first starred item, as opposed to a dash or other marking, says: "The Muslim civilian population continues ..." I won't read it further. But can you just describe to the Chamber the kind of information that was coming to the Spanish battalion at this time and in fact whether this report reflects that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL
utterances.text: This report could have been supplied both by my patrol, which was in Mostar, and by the section over the APC's, which were also patrolling in Mostar and with the direct contact with both sides since we had the possibilities. In spite of all the limitations and the shelling and all the rest, we could nevertheless, we could at times get to either the east or the west side.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I'm skipping over a number of documents, but there's one that's not in the binder. And if I could have the usher's assistance please. The document which has been marked as 429.1, if those could be distributed, please. Mr. Usher, if I could have one extra one back. I have one but for Mr. Stringer. Thanks very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Witness LL, this is an ECMM report, but your name, I believe, is mentioned in it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Meek.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honour, a couple of things: One, has this document been translated into the native tongue of my client to date? And secondly, it appears that this exhibit, P429.1, involves an area, location that is clearly outside of this indictment.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Your Honour, on the translation issue, no, it has not. It has not yet been translated. It will be submitted for translation. And as to the location, there has been extensive testimony, indeed, on Stolac, and it is directly related to the course of conduct in this case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: So you may proceed, Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Now, this document will have to be under seal because the witness name is mentioned, so I don't want to look at that or give that information, Witness LL. But you apparently had reported this information to the ECMM. And can you tell us, briefly, what happened on about the 9th of May at this medical centre in Stolac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL
utterances.text: Well, what I will -- what is said here was not said by me directly. It was a source which informed me about what had happened, and who also said -- and who went with me to the hospital in Stolac. I went with him there. He showed me photographs of patients who were in this hospital earlier, and he told me that they had been displaced, evicted by the HVO forces and that these people had been transferred in an unknown direction. Now, this person who gave me all this detail was also afraid for the lives of these people, that is, sick people, disabled people, elderly people. And I merely made a report to my superior so that all these details could be investigated, gone into in greater depth.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And do you know whether, in fact, after this time, that this incident was investigated and confirmed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL
utterances.text: I do not. I reported to my superiors, and personally, I was not put in charge of this investigation. I tried to supply all the information, that is, the names of people and doctors and everybody else who worked there in this hospital, so as to -- and hoping that that would be of help to my superiors.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Let me ask you this before moving on, then, to a last document or two: Did you, the Spanish army, did you cooperate, in fact, with a number of international organisations who were also on the ground at that time, such as the European Community Monitoring Mission?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL
utterances.text: Yes, we cooperated with other humanitarian organisations.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, I do want to conclude the witness before the lunch break. And of course, the Chamber will have all the exhibits, of course, the ones that are admitted, to review, so I think I will not put further documents in front of the witness. Witness LL, I thank you very much for your testimony.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I should also like to thank everybody here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Any cross-examination, or you prefer to do it some time later?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It will be Mr. Meek who will be cross-examining the witness, but it is only five minutes before the break, so I do not know whether it's really worth starting it now. Perhaps we should do it after the break, but it is, of course, up to you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We'll resume at 2.30 this afternoon. --- Luncheon recess taken at 12.55 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Meek.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Witness LL. How are you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL
utterances.text: Good afternoon to you. I'm very well, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: My name is Mr. Chris Meek, and I'm one of the attorneys representing Mr. Naletilic.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL
utterances.text: Nice to meet you. My name is LL.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: LL, it is very nice to meet you too. I met a comrade of yours, JJ, the other day, and he was a very nice gentleman also.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: May we go to private session briefly?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. We'll go to the private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: May I have the usher help me here with an exhibit to place on the ELMO. For the record, it would be Exhibit P2. Could you zoom it out.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Witness LL, the Prosecutor, right before the lunch break, handed us an Exhibit marked P429.1, a one-page document which involved an incident in Stolac. Do you recall that document and that testimony, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Would you please review the Exhibit P2 which is on the ELMO and point for the Trial Chamber where the town of Stolac is located on that map?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL
utterances.text: Here, exactly here, because we can read the name "Stolac" on the map.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: You might take that closer. Take it off the ELMO and read that and tell me again if that is Stolac.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL
utterances.text: Exactly to the west of Mostar, south-west of Mostar.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Do you see the city on that map, Witness?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL
utterances.text: Could you repeat your question, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Yes. I'm just asking you, do you see the city of Stolac, S-t-o-l-a-c, on this map Exhibit P2?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL
utterances.text: No. No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Would you agree with me -- and take your time, Witness, and look at the whole map.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL
utterances.text: Now, do you want me to tell you where Stolac is? This is how I understood your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: You understood my question correctly, sir.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL
utterances.text: I think that the Stolac city could be found near Blagaj, around here.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: I take it that you are not certain where the city of Stolac is located. Would that be a fair statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL
utterances.text: Well, yes, it is right. I have to see exactly a map with -- road map in order to identify the exact location of Stolac.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Witness LL, while I am looking for a larger map for you, would you take a marker and outline the area in which you had command authority during your stay in Bosnia-Herzegovina in 1993, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL
utterances.text: Can I draw on this map that I have been given? Could I draw on this map?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Yes, sir, you may.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL
utterances.text: I think I have marked and underlined the area that approximately -- the approximate area where I was able to travel during my stay in Bosnia-Herzegovina from January to June 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: And can the technical people zoom that out a little bit so we can see the whole map. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: On the bottom right of the map, you have a line, and then you have marked through it. Was that a mistake, Witness?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL
utterances.text: Yes. Because if not, we will be going into the Serbian area. However, with Colonel -- one of the colonels of the HVO in Capljina, I was able to visit the part of Stolac and there, he explained that it was an important area where there was combat between the -- in the Apura Battle between the two contending forces. And please, take into account that if I draw on this map, I make a line on this map, it could be several kilometres. And this would be quite different if we had a scale of, for instance, 1 per 5.000.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I'm asking for clarification and assistance. The number of the exhibit that this is based on, please, the one that's on the ELMO now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We also have some doubts about the number of this map, because it seems different from the --

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: The P2 I have, Your Honour, is quite different, in a very material way, in which this witness was just cross-examined.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Wait a minute. Momento. I apologise for any confusion. I have Exhibit 2 on the bottom of this map that the witness is looking at that was given to us by the -- my apologies. Mrs. Registrar shows me P2. This is a map that was originally Exhibit 2.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, would you please take this map and show it to the Prosecutor to make sure it's the same map we are looking at. No, no, no, not this one; that one.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Can I inquire, is this the map that was just put to the witness about finding Stolac? Was there an earlier map, or is this Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. the only map -- I'm sorry, Your Honour, I don't mean to converse with counsel, but I do want to seek some clarification in terms of if this is the only map that has been put in front of the witness so far.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We also need the explanations from Defence counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I explain. Mr. Scott is right. This is the only map that has been placed in front of this witness since lunch, and perhaps all day. I humbly apologise for stating that it was P2. It was my mistake. I saw the Exhibit Number 2, and this is how we received the exhibit from the Prosecutor. Perhaps this map has never been introduced into evidence to date.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, I think what's happened here, I think maybe as an earlier exercise, perhaps even during the depositions or something, there may have been -- at some point there may have been a version like this, although I don't remember offhand. But I'll allow for that possibility. However - and I'm being very objective here - I'm not prepared to cast any stones in any direction at the moment. But P2 is a different map, and it has the municipality of Stolac on it. Now, to put the other map in front without Stolac and put the witness through some paces to say, "Please find Stolac for me," when Stolac was not on that map is a little unfair to the witness, I submit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We also believe that we could agree with the Prosecutor. You cannot set a trap and ask the witness to fall into this trap.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Your Honours, I again humbly apologise. I was not attempting to do that in any fashion. And if Madam Registrar would show the witness what actually is P2, then I can ask my question. But again, for the record, it's just a mistake. I believed this to be Exhibit 2. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: You have to promise me that this kind of mistake should be never repeated again in this courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Your Honour, I will promise you that I will never attempt to make such a mistake; I didn't mean to in the first place. Your Honour, I would add that part of my confusion is that I am not from Bosnia-Herzegovina, and I also have some problems with the logistics or geography.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: That's not a good excuse, Mr. Meek.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Your Honour, I agree with you. No excuse is a good excuse. It will not happen again.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Witness LL, now you're looking at what has been marked as P2, and you can see Stolac, can you not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL
utterances.text: Yes. And I apologise as well, because I'm a military man and I should have known exactly, without any doubt whatsoever, where Stolac was, because I went there several times. But a military map is quite different from this drawing which was shown to me at first, and I had no references, and ten years later it's rather difficult to remember exactly where the different cities were located. Thank you very much. Here it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: And Witness LL, on the previous map that you drew the marks on showing your area of responsibility, did --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Meek, we could not accept the previous map. You have to ask this witness to draw it again on the P2.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Okay. Might I ask the Trial Chamber, is this a clean map right now? I don't want the witness to mark on it if it's going to be inappropriate.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This is a clean copy.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Is it appropriate to mark on it?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Witness LL, with all my sincere apologies, could you do what you did earlier and take the green marker and outline your area of responsibility when you were in Bosnia-Herzegovina in 1993.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL
utterances.text: Yes. Now, my area of responsibility was the area of responsibility of the Malaga Tactical Group of the Spanish forces, and I'm going to mark this area approximately just now. This is the east area of all this drawing here we could not occupy, because at that time there was a Serbian front. This Lasar [phoen] is a city that had been -- where there was a lot of struggling before we arrived. The Serbian front was rather more to the east. And in the northern area, it almost reached Sarajevo, but we could not take the general road because the Serbian part with Mladic was occupying all this area of Tarcin. And this is -- here we went to Kresevo, and then we went to Sarajevo here through the north. This is a mountainous ridge up to here, Kiseljak approximately. I was able to move about, and then I went down through Jablanica towards the west, Siroki Brijeg. I don't remember exactly if I could go towards the west, which was the area under the responsibility of the Spanish group, Ljubuski, Capljina. And even at the beginning, because our unit was in Ljubuski, we used the road from Ljubuski Polje and Stolac -- I'm sorry, Capljina, Dracevo in order to escort convoys of UNPROFOR up to Sarajevo. And this, it can be summarised, is the Neretva Valley. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Witness. Now, my next question would be, then: Was the city of Stolac within your zone of responsibility or the Malaga group's zone of responsibility?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL
utterances.text: Well, I don't remember exactly whether it was at the very limit, whether we could go to visit it, but I was able to go there with Colonel Radovic. And I believe that from Stolac, it's where contacts began with the Serbian part to start working for peace with the Serbs, to get rid of the mines and to put down the mines. And we did -- with the Serbian counterpart, we brought either dead bodies or prisoners for exchange, this by request from the HVO or the HV army. And Stolac was a sort of corridor that allowed for conversations to take place with the Serbian groups.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Witness. Since you were there in Bosnia-Herzegovina for a number of months in 1993, could you take a red marker and mark on the same map, P2, the area on that map that was occupied by the Muslim forces.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL
utterances.text: The most important thing that I think I remember is that it was concentrated on the eastern side of Mostar, the Ivar River [phoen], even though the HQ of Armija was on the western side. But I know that on the south of Mostar, there was an area that was the responsibility of the Muslims, the Armija forces, in order to defend the Serbian front because there was an agreement between these two groups in order to share this sector of monitoring this area, which was a sort of Serbian front. Now, the Muslim area before Jablanica, approximately here, there was a majority of Muslims. And also there were some Muslim checkpoints as well. Tacin is also in the Muslim area. And here, there is a ridge, and on the other side, there's a city, Kresevo, where there were a lot of Bosnians and Croatians; and Kiseljak, where the majority, if I remember correctly, Bosnians and Croatians. And the first period before the conflict broke out, I think I remember there was a good sharing of areas under the responsibility in order to defend the Serbian front, and this was the main concern. And this I realised in the first few months where I was in Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Witness, you mentioned Jablanica, and you indicated that perhaps that was a Muslim-controlled area. Did I understand that correctly or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL
utterances.text: In Jablanica, the majority population was Muslim. There were also armed forces, military, and paramilitary Muslim forces there. And the same goes for Konjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Witness LL, thank you -- can you take the red marker and mark the areas that was Muslim controlled. That's what I'd like you to do, if you can.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL
utterances.text: You are requesting for me major accuracy, and I really wouldn't dare do that in this area. I mentioned the chief nuclei , and around these nuclei were deployed military forces. But to draw it on this map, I would have to go through the documents in order to really establish where were the army force - that is, the BH army forces - deployed there with any accuracy. It is very difficult for me to do it quite accurately. I would have to look first at the military map to go from one point to the other, and very carefully, and then see if I could, perhaps, remember it correctly and accurately.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Thank you for your answer. And I understand that it has been nine years, and that your memory is not completely correct about everything. And I wouldn't ask you to give me exact locations. But if you can give me to the best of your memory today is all I'm asking. And if you have no memory as of today, just tell me, and I'll go on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DIARRA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, there is something which disturbs me with this analysis. He just said that he would feel more comfortable with a military map where all the routes are traced rather than with this schematic map, the Defence. It is not because his memory is faulty that he does not remember. I'd like you in your comments not to change the truth, what the witness has said.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What I am trying to say, that it is very difficult -- that it was very difficult to ascertain with any certainty whatsoever where the units were deployed. I had contacts with the different chiefs, with different commanders, but it was very difficult to deduce from what we heard about them where the troops were and what the forces were doing. There were HVO forces, there were BH army forces, and they were telling us about their problems, and different problems about the logistics, about their needs, humanitarian assistance, and so on and so forth. But to ascertain what was the deployment, it means that I would have to go from one point to another, and that was very difficult to say. So that the ORBATs that we had usually had very many question marks as to the exact locality. It was really intelligence work, which we could never do properly at the time when I was there. It was very difficult to come by any information, and I would never dare go into these details and ask about these details for -- and another thing is because I might fear to disclose the source of information that I had. It could also affect our security. And because I didn't want to do that, I concentrated on the area of Mostar. In Jablanica, there was another officer of mine, but it is really very difficult because this kind of information is very difficult to point at. And especially at the time, when all these operations were taking place, we were trying to follow and go to places and to concentrate on the places where we realised that people might be displaced from or where the population was suffering, where the population was victimised. But it was practically impossible to get to all the places where the actions were taking place.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Witness, we quite understand your difficulties, especially during the time of the war. The lines are not very clear, and it's after nine years, after all. So we'll kindly ask the Defence counsel to withdraw this question on this very issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: I was just about --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: And that way, Witness, you have to keep a little bit of distance from the mike so that we could hear you very clearly, because all the other people rely on the interpreters. Thank you. Mr. Meek.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness LL. I understand. I will not ask you any more questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: And I no longer need the ELMO at this point. So if it could be lowered, I would appreciate it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The marked map is entered as D1/33.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Witness LL, your force was a reconnaissance force; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: And earlier in a closed session, we spoke about Witness JJ. And his unit was an intelligence unit; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL
utterances.text: No, it is not. They were not doing intelligence work in that area but information, and this information was transmitted to Spain. We did not have a special intelligence unit to study this information and analyse it as an intelligence document, as an intelligence piece of work.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: So, LL, then you're saying that JJ's work was, then, gathering information and forwarding that information to the powers that may be in Spain but not intelligence gathering.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL
utterances.text: Yes, you are quite right. He was - how shall I call it? - the scribe of the second section of the Main Staff because he knew languages. So he was writing down the -- he was writing these reports and then Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. sending them on to our superiors.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: And would Witness JJ receive information from you and your unit to put into his reports?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL
utterances.text: Not to JJ but to the command, and the commander then gave it to him to copy it, to make a transcript, and to send it to the higher level.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: And were you ever, during your tenure in Bosnia-Herzegovina, were you ever at, physically at any meetings with military people from the HVO or BiH with him? Were you at any of the meetings he attended, if you recall?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL
utterances.text: I don't. I don't recall. Could be, because he was at the headquarters in Medjugorje. Perhaps at some of the meetings attended by HVO - BH army representatives came - or these representatives. It could be that such a meeting to which my superiors sent me, it is quite possible that he was also there. But I just do not recall it. Perhaps he was, but I just don't know it, but I cannot affirm really that he was personally present with me. I do not -- he merely -- possibly he escorted me, but we did not work together there. This sector -- perhaps he would be -- he would be taking videos or -- with buses with prisoners -- of buses with prisoners and things like that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: One point of clarification: I think that JJ, when he gave his evidence, said that he didn't take part in these high-level meetings. His job was to direct where the people were to go, and he played a very low-level role. He didn't take part in the meetings. And I think that your question somehow misrepresents what he said yesterday. I'd like you to clarify it with the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Thank you, Judge Clark. I had the same problem with Witness JJ. I didn't --

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Witness, when I meant -- I didn't mean that JJ would ever take part in meetings, but I just wondered whether you saw him around the area where the meetings were being conducted.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL
utterances.text: I cannot answer that because I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Witness, I appreciate that. And if I ask you a question today that you don't recall, just please tell me you do not recall it. Also, if I ask a question that you don't understand, please tell me that you don't understand the question and I'll try to rephrase it. Is that fair?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL
utterances.text: Thank you very much. What I'm doing is making a great effort to try to help the Defence when you ask me about Mr. Tuta, and I'm trying to be as accurate as possible, and I'm really sorry that perhaps at times I cannot help you as much as you would like me to.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Witness LL, you began your military training in what year, 1976?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL
utterances.text: I confirm, in 1976.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: And you have been, since that time, a professional soldier, and now you are a major; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: In your training and experience as a professional soldier, have you had training on making reports?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL
utterances.text: This is one of the many things, that we received information not only through reports but also in various military -- related military matters too.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: And in your training and experience as a military officer of high command, you understand the importance of making a complete report on any incident; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL
utterances.text: Yes, it is. That is how it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness LL, I must ask you how it came that you gave an interview on the 3rd of November of 2000 with individuals and representatives from the Office of the Prosecutor for this Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL
utterances.text: Because the Ministry of Defence of Spain decided so.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: So the Ministry of Defence in Spain came and asked you to give a statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: You didn't volunteer?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL
utterances.text: Well, yes. It is -- it is voluntary in a way. If the army tells me that I have to perform a task and to give my opinion about certain things that I personally went through and that I have to provide the facts, then I cannot deny that, because I indeed lived through that and because I'm asked to do that and to comply with it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Maybe there's some confusion in translation, but basically my question was: They came to you and asked you; you didn't come to them or go to them and ask them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL
utterances.text: Well, yes. I did not know that this gentleman had come to Spain to get a statement from me and other people in Spain. I wasn't all that in touch with the situation after ten years, and I didn't know that this was going on. I think that other commanders, my superiors, thought that it was I because of the contacts that I had with other people and my superiors had Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. contacts with in the area, and therefore they indicated people who perhaps could contribute information -- the Mostar information for this -- in this case.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Witness LL, when you gave your statement to the Office of the Prosecutor for this Tribunal, you were aware, were you not, that the statement would be used in the Prosecution of Mr. Mladen Naletilic, known as Tuta, did you not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL
utterances.text: Could I seek the advice of my legal counsel, possibly? Could it be possible?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Witness, you have to understand that your legal counsel here is to protect the interests of the State. If you believe that this question touches upon the interests of the State, you have full rights to consult with your legal counsel. But it seems to me it's just an ordinary question. Of course, the decision will be made by yourself. If you insist, we'll give you the opportunity.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL
utterances.text: Well, it was mostly to give as broad an answer that I can; that is, I wanted to add something to the knowledge that they have, to give as broad as possible an answer to this question. But be that as it may, I would say that yes, indeed, I knew that there was an investigator from the Prosecutor's office who had come to Spain related to this case. I did not know whether this would be used in favour -- against or for both parties.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Meek, is that the answer to your question?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: That's the answer to that question, Your Honour, yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Witness LL, once you -- let me ask this question: How long did the interview take for you to give your statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL
utterances.text: Well, more or less, it lasted like this session today. That is, we had part of it in the morning and part of it was in the afternoon. And we had a break for lunch, sufficiently long break for a decent lunch.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: At any point once the interview started did it become apparent to you that the individuals who were taking your statement were focussing or targeting Mr. Naletilic and what you knew about him specifically?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL
utterances.text: The truth is that everything began with general situation, and then slowly, gradually as I was telling more and more about my experience there and things that -- and my recollections, the investigator started to stop me and requesting that I belabour those particular aspects. But I was telling them about all my personal experience, about all that I went through with all the individuals whom I met during that time. And yes -- in those instances when I referred to HVO, to my contacts, my friends, yes, they sometimes requested more details. But I just told them all that because I knew very many people also from the BH army command. We also talked about the death of Mr. Hudruk who came from the BH army, so this story was practically a monologue about all the experience that I went through at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: And at those times that the investigators would stop you and, as you say, have you belabour a point about Mr. Naletilic, or Tuta, you told them everything you could remember, did you not?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Meek, you said "as you say." I could not recall that witness said something particularly in this direction.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Page 75, line 10.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Can you read the same sentence? I cannot see, you know, the meaning that was expressed by you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Your Honour, I apologise. I used the same word, at least, that the translator used when this witness indicated in his prior answers that while he gave his statement about all of his experiences, the investigators "started to stop me and requesting that I belabour those particular aspects."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, you may rephrase your question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DIARRA
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Witness LL, do you mean that when you would get to certain parts of your statement that involved Tuta, that they would stop you and have you be more specific about him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL
utterances.text: Yes. With him -- concerning him and all the other sources whom I had contact with in the BH army and the HVO. And I also remember that I explained about Humo and Hudruk and about all the military commanders that I named, asking how much knowledge, how much information, how well I knew each one of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: And to make the record clear, you arrived in Mostar in approximately March, is that correct, and left in July?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL
utterances.text: Permanently, yes. I arrived in Mostar in March and then stayed on, but my visits to Mostar were periodical. I came there from Jablanica trying to deal with various matters personally with the chief of the Main Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: And did you meet this individual by the name of Ivan Andabak prior to your locating in Mostar in March of 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL
utterances.text: Right now, I could not really say for certainty. I do not know whether it was before -- prior to that. I know that Colonel Zorzo, I went to the area. It could have been in mid-April. But right now, I cannot say with certainty whether it was before that dinner. Well, yes, somehow I think that I must have met him before and exchanged with him some words prior to that, because Mr. Andabak was a man who was very fond, and is very fond, of the Spanish forces. But whether it was before March or after March, later on -- there was, for instance, a Spanish car. He was a very human person, he had a good heart, and he loved Spain. And he addressed me in Spanish. So I really cannot really answer your question with complete precision -- with precision. But after, following that dinner, my relations with him and with other people who were at the dinner became closer because this first serious or noteworthy relationship had already started.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness LL. And I would just ask you when you answer, if you could maybe move a little bit back from the microphone. You're moving towards it again. Are you telling us today that your relationship with my client, Tuta, became closer after the dinner?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL
utterances.text: Well, it could not really become particularly close because I could not communicate with him as often as with other military colleagues in the HVO or the BH army. But I could greet him as sporadically, spontaneously when we would meet in the street, and to know physically who that was. And then I merely begin to trust people with whom I deal, and especially -- and to who had been introduced to me. And at that dinner, at that meeting, there was this atmosphere of friendship and trust.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Witness LL, thank you for that answer. But as I understand your testimony and as I understand your statement that you gave to the OTP, you only saw Mr. Tuta one time after this dinner very quickly on the street in Siroki Brijeg. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL
utterances.text: Right. Now, in Siroki Brijeg, I think it was more than once. I cannot remember. I'm quite sure that in Siroki Brijeg, it is quite true that it could be that it was on more than one occasion. But I cannot remember any other noteworthy meetings. There were more dinners with military sources - it is quite true - that I had. But I do not remember any other occasion that was as important as that one, as intensive as that one.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: I would ask the usher to hand the statement that Witness LL gave to the Office of the Prosecutor in November of 2000.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Witness LL, the first page of that document indicates - and I don't want you to tell me, obviously - but it tells your name and it says your occupation. It says the languages you speak, does it not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: And those two languages are Spanish and French; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Did you -- did you converse with my client, Tuta, in Spanish and/or French? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Do you know whether or not my client, Mr. Naletilic, speaks Spanish or French?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL
utterances.text: Perhaps he could say one sentence in Spanish, say "hello," "goodbye," a couple of words at most, but I don't know. A typical "salut" expressing friendship, that is all.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Could you turn to page 6 of that statement? And the third paragraph from the top, the very first sentence. May you have your -- I don't -- do you speak any English, Witness?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL
utterances.text: No. I'm very sorry, but I cannot understand English directly.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Please don't be sorry. I speak no Spanish. And by the way, this morning you didn't insult me whatsoever in not being able to pronounce names. I have the same problem. Could you have the interpreter read that first sentence for you. Paragraph 3.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL
utterances.text: Yes, the first sentence is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: That is a correct statement of the facts?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: What is the --

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: I'm getting to that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: In that sentence, you said: "I met Tuta once more in Siroki Brijeg on the street." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: And prior to that, you making that statement, you giving that sentence, you had talked about meeting Tuta at the dinner party at Andabak's house; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: So then will you agree with me that you only met my client two times?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Your Honour, that's an unfair --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: He said "you met him twice in Siroki Brijeg." It's unfair to say, "Does that mean you only met him two times?" He could have met him somewhere else.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Meek, do you hear the objection from the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Yes, I did. Let me rephrase my question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: When you stated to the Office of the Prosecutor in November of 2000 that you met Tuta one more -- once more in Siroki Brijeg on the street, what did you mean?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL
utterances.text: Yes. What I mean to say is that once again in Siroki Brijeg, comma, on the street. I mean that it's the second time that I meet him in Siroki Brijeg, and this time I met him on the street.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Thank you. And the first time you met him in Siroki Brijeg was at the dinner party at Mr. Ivan Andabak's house; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: The month of that party, I believe you've indicated, was sometime in April of 1993. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL
utterances.text: Yes. I'm sorry, I wanted to say something. The house of Ivan Andabak was in Siroki Brijeg. That's why I repeated once again "in Siroki Brijeg."

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: After the meeting in Siroki Brijeg on the street that you indicate on page 6, did you ever meet Mr. Naletilic again?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL
utterances.text: Yes. I saw him at some opportunity very quickly on passing -- in passing at HQ of HVO. But as I do not know exactly the day and the month, I don't think it's really important, at least not for me. So I mentioned this event because we stopped on the street to say hello.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: So after the meeting on the street in Siroki Brijeg where you said hello and testified in direct examination that it was a very brief meeting, you never spoke to Mr. Naletilic, Tuta, again, did you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL
utterances.text: Well, after I met him in Siroki Brijeg, I don't remember. After this time when we met on the street, I don't remember that I ever spoke to him in a direct fashion. I just don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: And you just testified under oath that you think you remember or you did remember seeing Tuta at the HVO headquarters, did you not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: And is that the same headquarters and the buildings you described this morning that Ivan Andabak had his offices?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL
utterances.text: It's the building where I saw Andabak once at a table. I think it was in his office. And I saw other military men from the HVO. And I remember that once in passing I saw him either going into or coming out of the building, because there was a parking lot for cars, and I saw him going into the building or out of the building. I don't remember exactly, but sporadically.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: And again, to clear up your answer - and perhaps it's in the translation - you are referring to Ivan Andabak's offices at the headquarters of the HVO in Mostar that was located on the same street as the cathedral of Mostar was situated?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Could you please turn to page 3 of your statement to the OTP and go to the second full paragraph and ask your translator to please read you or translate for you the last sentence of that second full paragraph. Witness LL, you told the office of the OTP in November of 2000 that, among other things, you tried to see Andabak every two or three days to get information; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL
utterances.text: Well, I tried to set up contact not only with Ivan Andabak but also with other military people from HVO - one of them was Andabak - and also with forces of the BH army to see what was going on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Thank you. But I'm looking at your statement. You did try to see Andabak every two or three days to get information; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL
utterances.text: Yes. This is correct, because it's quite easy to have contacts and know Spanish.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: And you also stated that you tried to bond with him and that you did it openly.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: And you told that he would always welcome you to his place, especially at the headquarters that was located on the same street as the cathedral of Mostar; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: And then you told the office of the OTP that you did not remember seeing Tuta in his office, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Thank you. How many people were at the dinner party in Siroki Brijeg at the house of Ivan Andabak that you have described today in your testimony?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL
utterances.text: Well, how many exactly? I think I remember on the Spanish side, Colonel Zorzo, his interpreter, Witness LL, Mr. Tuta, Mr. Ivan, his wife Juani. His daughter, I think, appeared at some point during the dinner party. An elderly person, I don't know whether she was Tuta's -- no, I'm sorry -- Ivan Andabak's mother or some relative of Ivan Andabak's. And bodyguards that I think were Ivan Andabak's bodyguards.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Meek, I don't believe there's a need for you to turn off your mike because we hear quite a noise through the earphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Shall I keep it on?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I think so. Because this witness is not under the protection of voice distortion.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: In the last answer when you were naming the people that were at the dinner party, you mentioned LL. Did you mean JJ?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL
utterances.text: I meant myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Okay. I knew you were there. And the question, the other people that were there, I wondered when you mentioned LL if you actually meant JJ.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL
utterances.text: No, I meant myself, my person.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Do you recall about what time that party started and what time the party broke up?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL
utterances.text: Well, I know that it was in the late afternoon. The sun had set. But this is not valuable information because I believe that the sun sets from 5.00 p.m. or 6.00 p.m. And we finished rather late at night. I don't know. Over midnight or at 1.00 a.m. I don't know. I'm trying to specify the hour. I don't remember the exact hour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Of course not, not eight years later, nine years later. Do you recall, Witness LL, if everybody at the party enjoyed themselves with food and drink?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL
utterances.text: Yes, there was no problem at all within the limitations set by the fact that we had to eat and drink with precaution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Meek, what a peculiar question you asked. Is that relevant to this case, whether they enjoyed their drink?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: The next question is relevant, Your Honour. I had to set the stage for my next question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: How much did you drink that night, LL?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL
utterances.text: Well, I don't -- I usually don't drink much when I am wearing my uniform, and I'm not a drinking man. I don't like alcohol very much, so I take as little as I possibly can. Sometimes there's a toast or there's something to -- some alcohol during dinner. But I don't remember. And I know that when I left, I wasn't dizzy or anything like that, because a military man shouldn't give this image to others.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: So you drank enough alcohol that you did not become dizzy, but you did drink alcohol that night; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL
utterances.text: Well, sincerely, I cannot say. I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Well, the reason I ask is because apparently, according to your testimony today, approximately two days later, you typed up or generated a report that concerned my client, Tuta. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: And did you do anything between the date of the dinner party and your generating of this report, which concerned my client, to corroborate any of the information contained in that report?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL
utterances.text: Yes, I believe that I explained this perfectly in the statement you got.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL
utterances.text: You've got it with you, haven't you?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Yes, I do. And I would like you, if you could, to turn to page 6 again of that report, since you explained everything in it, the sixth paragraph down. Can you read it to him. Witness LL, you told the Office of the Prosecutor investigators in November of last year that, "I had all the information about Tuta from Andabak." Isn't that what you told the Office of the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL
utterances.text: But the first person --

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: What I'm wondering about --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL
utterances.text: Please. The first person that gave me exact data about his life was him, in trust. And then this information I completed later on, thanks to data of Ivan Andabak and other sources -- military sources of HVO that were close to Tuta gave me. But I could not obtain any information about Tuta earlier on because I had never met him and I didn't know exactly that he existed at all. And it was him, Tuta, himself in a very friendly fashion in full trust gave me all this data. And as from that time, I wanted to hear about Mr. Tuta, his friend that he had introduced me to; and therefore, I completed all the data on him thanks to Ivan Andabak and other sources of information of HVO. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: So, what you're telling us today is that after the dinner party, in the next 48 hours or 2 days, you talked to Ivan Andabak and other military sources of the HVO that were close to Tuta before you generated the report that you generated. Is that what happened?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL
utterances.text: No, not exactly. Because this report, I think I remember at least that when I got to Medjugorje, I started drafting this report, even though this report was handed over two days later. But the first thing I did was to draft it, and this is what I usually do in order to remember exactly what happened, all the data.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Did you get back to your headquarters in Medjugorje that evening?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: And you started working on the report that night?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL
utterances.text: Normally, this is what I usually do. I never leave it for the next day. At least the first few important notes, the key ideas, I put them down on paper. And then perhaps the next day I complete the information with some details. But the main ideas, I usually write them Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. down immediately and even, sometimes, in my own personal agenda.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: What do you mean by your own personal agenda?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL
utterances.text: Well, I mean, it's a personal notebook I carry with me to jot down ideas that occur to me, and then I take notes. I jot them down.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: It's just a matter of language, Witness LL. You mean like a diary.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL
utterances.text: No, it's not a diary, because there's a diary of operations. It's just a notebook where I write down a few ideas, four or five key ideas, and then I later develop them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Do you still have that notebook today?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: And then in the few days it took you to complete this report, you spoke with Ivan Andabak again?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL
utterances.text: We are talking about this dinner party that took place approximately -- according to the documents we can look at, it took place at the beginning of April, on the 5th or 6th of April. And now, at this point, I cannot remember two days later whether I spoke to Ivan Andabak. It's impossible for me to tell you just now whether it was two days later. I just don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: I'm trying to understand your testimony, Witness LL. And if I'm wrong, correct me. But I believe in direct examination you testified that the report was generated and handed in approximately two days after the dinner party.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: And this afternoon, you've told me under oath that before it was finished, you had spoken with Andabak and other close HVO acquaintances of Mr. Tuta. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I object, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I think that's a mischaracterisation of the testimony completely.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Let me ask it a different way.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Witness LL, did you speak with any person, or persons, between your first meeting at the dinner party at Ivan Andabak's home where you met Tuta and when you turned in this report that concerned Tuta?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL
utterances.text: Sincerely, I cannot remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: You indicated in your direct testimony that as an overall assessment of reliability on the reports that you did for the military staffs, you took information from both members of the HVO and the ABiH army and civilians; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL
utterances.text: This is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: And you indicated that perhaps they would tell you good details if they wanted to tell you the truth.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL
utterances.text: It is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Do you believe that there is -- strike the question. I want to ask a different question. You also indicated that when you first met Ivan Andabak, you and he talked about being in the same line of business or counterparts; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Witness LL, did it ever occur to you that Ivan Andabak would lie to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL
utterances.text: Not only Andabak but any other sources, they cannot [as interpreted] lie.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: What do you mean "they cannot lie"? They can lie.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Well, that's not what it says in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL
utterances.text: I believe that something happened in the translation of my words. The sources can always lie. It's -- it depends on the degree of trust, on what they want to tell us. So normally there's a contrast, work done with the information coming from other sources.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Thank you, LL. And I think I have time for one further question before we break today. Your life experiences and common sense tell you that it's very rare indeed that a person can meet another person for the very first time in their life and gain complete trust from that person; isn't that a fact?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS LL
utterances.text: I'm not like that. I normally, usually trust people I talk to, because I open myself to them, and I think that others do the same. This has been my experience. Perhaps it has made me carry out mistakes, but if I look at people's eyes, if I'm invited to their homes, if we speak in a friendly atmosphere, I do not think that these people are lying to me. I try to help this person, I try to understand them. And we were there to help everybody. And sometimes this could affect my life, but I think that being sincere is the first thing you have to do when you talk to other people.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: That is an excellent way to live your life, Witness LL, but will you agree with me that not everybody lives their life as you do and trusting immediately?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Meek, we have to stop here.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krsnik. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Thank you, Your Honour. I wanted to raise two things. The first is the confusion with maps. I'm the one to be held responsible for it, because the binder that the Prosecution gave us - and these are exhibits from 1 to 52 - includes the map that Mr. Meek -- the first map that Mr. Meek showed, without the municipality of Stolac. And this binder was given us at the time of depositions, from your learned friends in the Prosecution. The binder that we were given at the beginning of this case, including exhibits from P1 to P60, includes the same map but with the Stolac municipality included. And therefore, in conclusion, we have two identical maps that were given by the Prosecution. One is with and one is without the municipality of Stolac, and we just oversaw that. And the second issue I wish to raise - but I do not want to waste your time because it's already past 4.00 - I'd just like to remind you of the request I made regarding our tomorrow's work. If you have already decided, if not, then never mind. I'll decide what to do later on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, this morning we heard an oral request from Mr. Krsnik asking not to sit on Friday afternoon. The reason of this request is that he may be absent during that period. This Trial Chamber could not accept this reason since each Defence team has its co-counsel to look after the interests of their client. As I understood, Mr. Meek is very competent in defending his client's interests and rights before this Chamber. As for whether we are going to sit or not tomorrow afternoon, it all depends on the ongoing proceedings of this case. As a principle, in order to avoid the contamination of the witness, we would not like to have a witness under oath for a long period without appearance in the courtroom. This is also for the interest of justice and fairness before this Chamber. So if we cannot finish with this witness, as well as the previous witness, Witness KK, we have to sit tomorrow afternoon. Thank you. We will adjourn until 9.30 tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Friday, the 9th day of November, 2001, at 9.30 a.m.
